answer: Agents anchor identity to a shared high-frequency sensor tide — each must continuously hash local readings of a volatile physical feed (power-grid harmonics, radio noise) into a rolling commitment chain; the network cross-correlates chains to detect synthetic identities, since faking N distinct but statistically independent views of the same nectar-rich entropy source costs O(N) storage and bandwidth per fake agent, while yarrow-rooted timing jitter in honest hardware makes coordinated simulation infeasible without physical presence at each node.
